symbols.description: capital letter A in normal orientation, with crossbar (slightly slanted handwriting); same glyph as 'A' in Z408/Z340
capital letter E in normal orientation (not reversed); same glyph as 'E' in Z408/Z340
capital letter N in normal orientation (diagonal runs top-left to bottom-right, not reversed); same glyph as 'N' in Z408/Z340

crosshairs / gunsight (the Zodiac's signature sign): a small open circle crossed by one vertical and one horizontal stroke, both extending well beyond the circle; webtoy code 'z' ('zodiac' glyph), the same symbol that occurs in Z408 and Z340

letter-sized closed circle drawn with a heavy outline, containing an inner figure: a small loop or arc in the upper half above a lower part split into two small compartments, so the whole reads like a circled '8' or a circled Taurus sign; the inner strokes differ slightly among the three instances; not one of the filled, half-filled or dotted circles of Z408/Z340; webtoy code '0' ('taurus', listed by Oranchak as a symbol unique to Z13/Z32)
capital letter K in normal orientation (not the reversed K that the convention writes as 'k'); same glyph as 'K' in Z408/Z340
capital letter M in normal orientation; same glyph as 'M' in Z408/Z340

inverted-T-like glyph: a vertical stroke coming down onto a short horizontal base whose right end curves upward into a hook (an upside-down T with the right arm turned up; variously called an upside-down or reversed J, an 'anchor', or the Aries sign); webtoy code '[' ('t2', listed by Oranchak as unique to Z13/Z32); resembles, but is not drawn like, the plain upside-down T ('t') of Z408/Z340

uncertainties: Circled symbols at positions 4, 6, 8 ('0'): every published transcription treats them as one repeated symbol, but their inner strokes differ slightly from copy to copy in the available scans, and no scan resolves the interiors with certainty. Readings in the literature: a circled '8' (Oranchak, Kelleher, most forum posts), a circled Taurus sign (Tom Voigt; an H. Davis comment on zodiackillerciphers.com, 2012), the Cancer sign (Ziraoui, 2021), an '8-ball' (T.C./'SDS' blog, 2025). Some typed renderings use a circle with an X. In this ASCII convention '8' means the filled triangle of Z408/Z340, so the circles must not be typed as '8'.

Glyph at position 9 ('['): Oranchak's convention gives it its own code ('t2'), distinct from the plain upside-down T ('t') of Z408/Z340. Several analysts equate it with that symbol instead: Oranchak's 2012 Lafferty critique notes a similar Z408 symbol decoding to R, and T.C. (2025) uses the Z340 upside-down T, which decodes to L. Others read it as a different symbol or letter: Lafferty (2012) and Ziraoui (2021) as the Aries sign, Garlick (2020/2025) as P, and Oranchak's 2012 article lists a plain T as an option. If it equals Z408/Z340 't', the key carry-over gives R (Z408) or L (Z340) at position 9.

Crosshairs at position 3 ('z'): identical to the signature the Zodiac drew on his letters, including the score line ('=10') on page 2 of this same letter. It may be an ordinary cipher symbol (it is one in Z408 and Z340) or a signature, separator or null. Lafferty (2012) replaced it with the letter Z, and T.C. (2025) treats it as punctuation.

Letter-shaped symbols (A, E, N, K, M): a strict substitution reading treats them as cipher symbols like any other. Some analysts read them as plaintext letters (TheDecipherist 2026 keeps A, E, N, M), and Tom Voigt suggested ignoring the first seven symbols as a copy of a Greek inscription (ANETHEKE).

Reading order: written as a single left-to-right line with no spaces. Nothing in the letter indicates transposition, but Z340 used transposition, so a non-linear reading order cannot be excluded (arXiv 2403.17350, section 8.2.1).

Scan quality: the best available scan is a binarized 640x829 copy (Wikimedia Commons File:Zodiac-name.gif, originally from zodiackiller.com). The colour scan on zodiackillerfacts.com is only 407x576. No high-resolution colour scan of the original was found online.

Date: Wikipedia and Wikisource give the postmark as April 20, 1970. On the zodiackillerfacts.com envelope scan the postmark reads 'AM / 2? APR / 1970'; the day digits are blurry, but the reading is consistent with 20 APR.

key_carryover.method: Decodings counted from position-aligned ciphertext/plaintext pairs: Z408 from AZdecrypt 'Zodiac 408.txt' + 'Zodiac 408 solved.txt' and doranchak/zodiac-cipher-key-visualizer z408.txt + z408-pt.txt (both agree); Z340 from the visualizer's z340-untransposed.txt + z340-untransposed-pt.txt (cross-checked against z340.txt + z340-pt.txt and Oranchak's combined key image).

E.z408: E (9 of 9 literal; Oranchak's annotated Harden key counts one as an enciphering slip for S)

N.z408: E (6 of 6 literal; Harden's worksheet reads one occurrence as T, which Oranchak attributes to a confused symbol)

[.z408: absent (the similar plain upside-down T 't' decodes to R, 7 of 7)
[.z340: absent (the similar 't' decodes to L, 4 of 4)

notes: Letter to the San Francisco Chronicle, postmarked April 20, 1970. Page 1 begins 'This is the Zodiac speaking', asks whether the last cipher (Z340, mailed November 8, 1969) has been cracked, writes 'My name is' followed by a dash, and then gives the 13 symbols on a line of their own.
Segmenting the cipher line of the Commons scan by column gaps gives exactly 13 glyphs in one row (see data/images/z13_glyphs_magnified_from_commons.png).

Structure: 13 symbols, 8 distinct. Repeats: the circled glyph 3 times (positions 4, 6, 8, symmetric about the centre position 6), A twice (0, 11), N twice (2, 10), M twice (7, 12). Oranchak (2012) notes that neither Z408 nor Z340 has this many repeats in any 13-symbol window.

Six of the 8 distinct symbols (A, E, N, z, K, M) also occur in Z408 and in Z340. The circled glyph '0' and the hooked upside-down T '[' occur in neither. Per AZdecrypt's 'Zodiac 32.txt' (C9J|#Ok[AMf8?ORTGX6FDVj%HCELzPW9), Z32 shares A, E, M, z and '[' with Z13.

Under the Z408 key, Z13 reads WEED?S?H??EWH; under the Z340 key it reads DREA?A?O??EDO. Neither key covers the circled glyph or '['. Several post-2020 proposals start from the Z340 reading: Garlick (DREATATOTPEDO), Ziraoui (KAYR) and T.C. (ANDREA J ODELL).

Under strict 1:1 substitution, only about 1 in 12 million random 13-letter strings fits the pattern abcdefegehcag (Oranchak, 2013). Scanning about half a billion name combinations, Oranchak found 213 that fit. Dictionary searches give thousands of fitting phrases, so a fit alone proves nothing. https://zodiackillerciphers.com/my-name-is-sarah-the-horse/

Possible trigger: on October 22, 1969 the San Francisco Examiner ran a challenge from D.C.B. Marsh, president of the American Cryptogram Association, daring the Zodiac to put his name in a cipher (Pelling 2017, https://ciphermysteries.com/2017/12/16/zodiac-killers-z13-cipher-meets-z340-cipher).
Side note for the Z408 file (not used for Z13): the AZdecrypt and key-visualizer Z408 transcriptions differ only at 0-based index 105 ('I' vs '!'), and the webtoy and Cipher Explorer use '!'.

checked_against_images: data/images/z13_letter_top_zodiackillerciphers.jpg (colour photo of the top of page 1, 657x262; cipher line magnified 4x)
findings: All three images show the same 13 glyphs in one left-to-right row: A, E, N, crosshairs, circled glyph, K, circled glyph, M, circled glyph, hooked inverted T, N, A, M. The ascii string matches glyph for glyph.
A, E, N, K and M are normal-orientation capitals (none mirrored), so they take the upper-case codes; the lower-case codes of the convention are reserved for mirrored letters.
The crosshairs glyph (circle with both strokes extending beyond it) is the same sign as Z408/Z340 'z'.

The hooked inverted T at position 9 is the same glyph as Z32 position 7 (both have the upturned right end), so both files use '['. The Z340 't' instances in 0-based rows 4 and 10 of the Commons colour photo of the Z340 (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:4abc_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_Dripping_Pen_Card_November_8_1969_340_Cipher_COLOR.jpg) are plain perpendicular signs without the hook, as is the Z408 R / Z340 L sign in Oranchak's combined key image (http://zodiackillerciphers.com/images/z408-z340-combined-keys.png), so '[' is kept distinct from 't' as in Oranchak's convention.

The three circled glyphs look alike at the available resolution (heavy circle, 8-like or Taurus-like interior); they keep the single code '0'. In the convention '8' is the filled triangle, so they must not be typed '8'.
Derived fields (isomorph, counts, positions, in_z32/in_z408/in_z340) recomputed from ascii by tools/certify_ciphers.py; the only change was the new in_z32 flag.
